name: Arkansas

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Arkansas became the 25th state on June 15, 1836. Congress gave it 1 seat in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1840 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1840 census, Arkansas kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1850 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1850 census, Arkansas's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: 1860 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1860 census, Arkansas's House delegation grew from 2 to 3 seats.

events.title: 1870 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1870 census, Arkansas's House delegation grew from 3 to 4 seats.

events.title: Some members elected at-large
events.text: In the 43rd Congress (1873–1875), Arkansas elected one of its representatives statewide (at-large) and the rest by district.

events.title: 1880 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1880 census, Arkansas's House delegation grew from 4 to 5 seats.

events.title: Some members elected at-large
events.text: In the 48th Congress (1883–1885), Arkansas elected one of its representatives statewide (at-large) and the rest by district.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, Arkansas's House delegation grew from 5 to 6 seats.

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, Arkansas's House delegation grew from 6 to 7 seats.

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, Arkansas kept 7 seats in the House.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, Arkansas kept 7 seats in the House.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, Arkansas kept 7 seats in the House.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, Arkansas's House delegation shrank from 7 to 6 seats.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, Arkansas's House delegation shrank from 6 to 4 seats.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, Arkansas kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, Arkansas kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, Arkansas kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, Arkansas kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, Arkansas kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2021 map becomes law without signature
events.text: The legislature passed new congressional maps (HB 1982 and SB 743) on October 7, 2021. The governor declined to sign them, and they became law without his signature on October 13, 2021.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, Arkansas kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Simpson v. Thurston dismissed
events.text: Voters sued in federal court in 2022, alleging the 2021 map's division of Pulaski County was racially discriminatory. After the U.S. Supreme Court sent the case back for another look in June 2024, a three-judge court dismissed it again on September 11, 2024.

events.title: Christian Ministerial Alliance v. Jester
events.text: A second federal suit claimed the 2021 congressional plan was based mainly on race and intentionally discriminatory. On June 9, 2025, a three-judge court granted summary judgment to the state, finding the evidence did not warrant a trial.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.
